program: Whole unrestricted gift with a representative vitamin A core

nutshell.headline: Our conditional best estimate is about $8,000 per 10 global QALYs.
nutshell.body: We charge the whole unrestricted gift and quantify a judgmental 30% vitamin A core. Other health benefits remain unquantified. No SF or Bay health is credited—not because Helen Keller has no US programs, but because their marginal local health is unverified.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: In high-burden settings, inexpensive vitamin A delivery can reduce childhood illness and mortality.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: The unrestricted allocation and survival conversion are judgments. A very large randomized trial found no clear mortality reduction, and modern effectiveness varies by setting.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Current marginal allocation, funding room and age-specific mortality yield need better evidence. This is not a guaranteed offer.

programSection.body: Helen Keller International (EIN 13-5562162) works in nutrition, vitamin A delivery, neglected tropical diseases and vision, including US vision services. It is distinct from Helen Keller Services.

steps.title: Support the whole organization
steps.detail: General gifts are flexible. Its dedicated vitamin A page restricts gifts to that work; that is a different donation boundary.

steps.title: Represent one health pathway
steps.detail: The model assigns 30% of the marginal gift to vitamin A-equivalent health, leaving other outcomes unquantified.

steps.title: Compare against existing care
steps.detail: Government programs, donated medicine and other grants already fund substantial services; existing recipients are not automatically additional.

programSection.boundary: The core share is an analyst prior, not the audited vitamin A share or a second overhead haircut. All gift dollars remain in the numerator.

model.headline: A $10,000 unrestricted gift yields an estimated 12.4769 global QALYs.
model.body: The historical anchor is $3,500 per modeled life saved. Our finite conversion assumes 80% early and 20% older deaths, 40/20-year remaining trajectories and a 2.5-year event delay. These are explicit priors, not a measured VAS death-age mix, national life table or GiveWell QALY estimate.

inputs.label: Finite survival and utility

inputs.label: Gift-to-event delay
inputs.basis: Pipeline approximation, not observed current deployment.

inputs.label: Relative core-opportunity yield
inputs.basis: Transfers the already-adjusted historical anchor without stacking new generic coverage, efficacy or financing penalties.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Null core allocation or yield gives no finite positive price. Independently caused harm can remain when benefits are zero. Shared harms scale with provision; source-covered clinical harms are not deducted twice. No unmodeled lifetime, income or separate blindness credit is added.
model.fundingBoundary: A current unrestricted funding gap or allocation is not verified. Dedicated VAS giving is restricted and cannot be substituted silently. Government services, existing grants and capsules funded through Nutrition International and Canada form the baseline. Full resource costs remain unknown; annual in-kind accounting is not the marginal cost of this gift.

evidence.population: About one million children in northern India; 36 retinol versus 36 control blocks
evidence.result: Mortality ratio .96 (95% CI .89–1.03), p=.22; no clear all-cause mortality reduction.
evidence.transfer: Primary indexed evidence verified; challenges universal 20–30% mortality claims but does not exclude smaller benefits in different settings.

evidence.population: 2022–24 vitamin A opportunities; summary updated August 2026
evidence.transfer: Not a trial QALY result or ordinary-gift quote. Allocation and future survival are our separate judgments.

evidence.result: Modern mortality reduction modeled at 1–11%, versus 19% trial average.
evidence.transfer: New disease, dosing and publication-bias analyses matter. A 25-times moral-weighted benchmark claim cannot be converted directly into dollars per life or QALYs.

evidence.population: Historical expansion to new Nigerian states
evidence.result: Evaluator says it would likely have made a smaller grant, excluding two states later exited.
evidence.transfer: Geography and monitoring can change effectiveness; historical average is not guaranteed everywhere.

reservations: General gifts are not automatically restricted vitamin A funding.
Nutrition expenditure does not identify vitamin A's marginal allocation.
The large mortality-null trial and current-context uncertainty remain substantive.
US programs exist, but no verified marginal SF/Bay health share is assigned.
excludedBenefits: Other nutrition, neglected-disease, eye-health and US vision effects not quantified here.
Separate income, education or blindness gains on top of the mortality bridge.
Unverified SF/Bay spillovers or headquarters-based benefit allocation.
Healthcare savings treated as donor cash and unreconciled societal resources.
